derived.prompt: What was the development code name of the direct predecessor of Windows Vista?

So the direct predecessor of Windows Vista was not built on the Windows NT kernel: no (Windows XP was).

related.prompt: Was Windows XP the direct predecessor of Windows Vista?

So Windows XP was not the direct predecessor of Windows Vista: no.

Windows Vista is the direct successor of.why: Stated directly and often: Vista is introduced as the successor to Windows XP in its own article, in the XP article and in most histories of Windows. A model holds the sentence itself, and a version has one direct predecessor, so the edit overturns it.

sources.quote: It was the direct successor to Windows XP, released five years earlier, which was then the longest time span between successive releases of Microsoft Windows.

sources.query: Vista, the successor to Windows XP

The direct predecessor of Windows Vista.why: Text gives XP's code name Whistler and calls XP Vista's predecessor, but never names the code name of 'Vista's predecessor' as such. Common sense: people say 'Vista followed XP' and 'XP was code-named Whistler'; nobody says 'Vista's predecessor was code-named Whistler', although it is true.

The direct predecessor of Windows Vista.why: Whether Vista's predecessor introduced the Start menu is never asked in text; it follows from which version that is and from the Start menu's origin in Windows 95. Common sense: people say 'Vista followed XP' and 'the Start menu came with Windows 95'; nobody says whether Vista's predecessor introduced it, although it is true.

The direct predecessor of Windows Vista.why: XP is described as NT-based and as Vista's predecessor, but the kernel of 'Vista's predecessor' is not written as such. Common sense: people say 'Vista followed XP' and 'XP is NT-based'; nobody states the kernel of Vista's predecessor on its own, although it is true.
